# Akasha original Python reference

`upstream-golden.json` was generated by running the original, unmodified Python
core of [akashic-agent at 94027a5cce9fc494f20bb7931fddf26f1e15e8df](https://github.com/kachofugetsu09/akashic-agent/tree/94027a5cce9fc494f20bb7931fddf26f1e15e8df).
Its source hashes and Python/package versions are recorded in `metadata`.
The original MIT notice is in `LICENSE` and alongside the TypeScript port.

The fixture contains two learning sequences, fourteen retrieve/commit steps and
four queries before and after an actual JSON snapshot restore. It captures Turn
inputs, retrieval tickets, graph columns/topology, causal clock state, learning
events, context, source provenance and readout results. Additional cases cover
tokenization, sparsemax thresholds and ties, tail calibration, a 260-row mixed
float32/float64 feature calculation, and stale-ticket recomputation.
Six direct readout variants additionally cover contextual and independent
selection, inhibited-but-visible nodes, precomputed and freshly calculated
fields, plus original `math.erfc` values used by recurrence survival.

The source-only section runs upstream FeaturePool mathematics over document
feature records with no Turn closure or graph commit. This is an explicit host
adaptation: valid raw sources lacking a closed dialogue remain searchable.
The raw-source adapter excludes returned candidates with neither positive dense
nor positive BM25 evidence; empirical sparsemax background mass alone cannot
introduce an unrelated raw record. The host's singleton namespace additionally accepts positive direct dense/BM25
support because one document provides no empirical tail contrast; the original
Turn graph calibration is unchanged. The singleton behavior has separate literal
behavior tests rather than pretending it is an upstream graph result.

To regenerate, clone the upstream repository and check out the exact commit,
create an isolated Python 3.12 environment and install `numpy==2.5.4` and
`jieba==0.42.1`. Set `AKASHA_REFERENCE_ROOT` to that checkout, then run:

```powershell
python test/fixtures/akasha/export-reference.py
```

`--output <file>` selects a comparison output without replacing the checked-in
fixture. The exporter rejects a different upstream HEAD. Python is a development
reference tool and is never used as a production worker.

The TypeScript tokenizer uses pinned `@node-rs/jieba@2.0.4`, search mode with HMM,
and the original lowercase/chunk/minimum-length/frequency rules. Its native
dictionary has the same entry set but differs in byte ordering and one duplicate
line from Python jieba 0.42.1; this is reflected in the explicit lexical version.
The checked-in original Python tokenizer cases cover mixed text, ambiguity,
search terms, repetition and rare characters. Matching finite cases does not prove
universal segmentation equivalence. Python dictionary SHA-256 is
`7197c3211ddd98962b036cdf40324d1ea2bfaa12bd028e68faa70111a88e12a8`.

Isolated float64 feature comparisons allow absolute error `1e-10`.
Whole-cycle results include float32 propagation and allow error
`2e-6 + abs(expected) * 1e-8`, including accumulated graph values. Node/source identities, topology,
ordering, sparsity support and learning qualification remain exact. Numerical
tolerance does not permit a different recalled record or ranking.
